text: ARES requires a human preference validation set of approximately 150 to 300 annotated datapoints to compute confidence intervals via prediction-powered inference [S4][S5][S6]. In contrast, RAGAS uses GPT-3.5 as its judge with few-shot prompts that are not targeted for each evaluation domain [S1][S3]. The sources do not explicitly state the specific number of human annotations required for RAGAS, only noting that ARES is more data-efficient [S2]. ARES uses these human annotations to boost ranking accuracy, whereas RAGAS relies on its specific prompting strategy [S1][S3].
